### Changelog

URL: https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/changelog
Description: Release notes for SearchFn packages.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

SearchFn ships a coordinated set of packages. Each release notes which packages changed.

## 0.2.0 — 2026-03-11

### Breaking

- Removed the legacy aggregate adapters package.
- Split adapters into dedicated packages:
  - `@searchfn/adapter-contracts`
  - `@searchfn/adapter-memory`
  - `@searchfn/adapter-indexeddb`
  - `@searchfn/adapter-postgres`
  - `@searchfn/adapter-meilisearch`
  - `@searchfn/adapter-elasticsearch`
  - `@searchfn/adapter-opensearch`

### Migration

#### Package mapping

| Old | New |
| --- | --- |
| legacy aggregate | `@searchfn/adapter-memory` |
| legacy aggregate | `@searchfn/adapter-indexeddb` |
| legacy aggregate | `@searchfn/adapter-postgres` |
| legacy aggregate | `@searchfn/adapter-meilisearch` |
| legacy aggregate | `@searchfn/adapter-elasticsearch` |
| legacy aggregate | `@searchfn/adapter-opensearch` |

#### Import mapping

| Old | New |
| --- | --- |
| `import { MemoryAdapter } from "<legacy>"` | `import { MemoryAdapter } from "@searchfn/adapter-memory"` |
| `import { IndexedDbAdapter } from "<legacy>"` | `import { IndexedDbAdapter } from "@searchfn/adapter-indexeddb"` |
| `import { PostgresAdapter } from "<legacy>"` | `import { PostgresAdapter, getPostgresMigrationSQL } from "@searchfn/adapter-postgres"` |
| `import { MeilisearchAdapter } from "<legacy>"` | `import { MeilisearchAdapter } from "@searchfn/adapter-meilisearch"` |
| `import { ElasticsearchAdapter } from "<legacy>"` | `import { ElasticsearchAdapter } from "@searchfn/adapter-elasticsearch"` |
| `import { OpenSearchAdapter } from "<legacy>"` | `import { OpenSearchAdapter } from "@searchfn/adapter-opensearch"` |

## Versioning policy

- **Patch (0.x.y)**: bug fixes, doc improvements, perf wins that don't change behavior.
- **Minor (0.x.0)**: new features, new adapters, backwards-compatible additions to the SearchAdapter contract.
- **Major (x.0.0)**: contract changes, removed deprecated APIs, breaking changes to envelopes.

SearchFn is in 0.x — minor versions may include breaking changes when called out in this changelog.

## Coordinated releases

`@searchfn/*` packages share a version. Upgrading is per-package, but the same version across packages is the supported configuration. Mixing major versions across packages is not supported.

## Upgrade guides

- Major bumps include a `### Migration` section above with package/import/dependency mappings.
- Run `npm ls @searchfn/*` after an upgrade to confirm versions match across the tree.

## See also

- [Configuration](/docs/reference/configuration)
- [GitHub releases](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/releases)



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Client API

URL: https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/client
Description: Create and configure a SearchFn client for in-app search.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Creating a Client

Use `createSearchClient()` to create a search client. The client validates inputs, applies defaults, and delegates to the underlying adapter.

```typescript
import { createSearchClient } from "@searchfn/client";
import { MemoryAdapter } from "@searchfn/adapter-memory";

const client = createSearchClient({
  adapter: new MemoryAdapter(),
  defaults: {
    limit: 20,
    limitPerResource: 10,
    fuzzy: true,
  },
});
```

## Configuration

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `adapter` | `SearchAdapter` | Required. The search adapter to use. |
| `defaults.limit` | `number` | Default result limit for `search` calls. |
| `defaults.limitPerResource` | `number` | Default per-resource limit for `searchAll` calls. |
| `defaults.fuzzy` | `boolean \| number` | Enable fuzzy matching by default. Pass a number for edit distance threshold. |

## Methods

### `initialize`

Declare resources and their searchable fields. Call before indexing.

```typescript
await client.initialize?.({
  resources: [
    { name: "tasks", searchFields: ["title", "description"] },
    { name: "notes", searchFields: ["content", "tags"] },
  ],
});
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resources` | `InitializeResourceConfig[]` | Array of resource declarations with name and searchable fields. |

### `index`

Index a batch of documents into a resource.

```typescript
await client.index({
  resource: "tasks",
  documents: [
    { id: "t-1", fields: { title: "Ship docs", description: "Write the guide" } },
    { id: "t-2", fields: { title: "Fix bug", description: "Handle retries" } },
  ],
});
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resource` | `string` | Target resource name. |
| `documents` | `SearchDocument[]` | Documents to index. Each has an `id` and a `fields` record. |
| `signal` | `AbortSignal?` | Optional abort signal. |

### `search`

Search a single resource. Returns matching document IDs.

```typescript
const ids = await client.search({
  resource: "tasks",
  query: "docs",
  limit: 10,
  fuzzy: true,
  fields: ["title"],
  fieldBoosts: { title: 2.0 },
});
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resource` | `string` | Resource to search. |
| `query` | `string` | Search query string. |
| `fields` | `string[]?` | Restrict search to specific fields. |
| `limit` | `number?` | Max results to return. |
| `fuzzy` | `boolean \| number?` | Enable fuzzy matching. |
| `fieldBoosts` | `Record<string, number>?` | Per-field relevance boosts (adapter support required). |
| `signal` | `AbortSignal?` | Optional abort signal. |

**Returns:** `Promise<Array<string | number>>`

### `searchAll`

Search across multiple resources. Returns results with resource name, ID, and score.

```typescript
const results = await client.searchAll({
  query: "launch",
  resources: ["tasks", "notes"],
  limitPerResource: 5,
});

// [{ resource: "tasks", id: "t-3", score: 1.5 }, { resource: "notes", id: "n-1", score: 0.8 }]
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | `string` | Search query string. |
| `resources` | `string[]?` | Resources to search. Omit to search all initialized resources. |
| `fields` | `string[]?` | Restrict search to specific fields. |
| `limit` | `number?` | Max total results. |
| `limitPerResource` | `number?` | Max results per resource. |
| `fuzzy` | `boolean \| number?` | Enable fuzzy matching. |
| `fieldBoosts` | `Record<string, number>?` | Per-field relevance boosts. |
| `signal` | `AbortSignal?` | Optional abort signal. |

**Returns:** `Promise<SearchAllResult[]>` where each result has `resource`, `id`, and `score`.

If the adapter does not implement `searchAll` natively, the client runs per-resource searches concurrently and merges results with deterministic score-based ordering.

### `remove`

Remove documents from a resource by ID.

```typescript
await client.remove({
  resource: "tasks",
  ids: ["t-1", "t-2"],
});
```

### `clear`

Remove all documents from a resource.

```typescript
await client.clear("tasks");
```

### `dispose`

Release resources held by the adapter. After disposal, call `initialize()` again before further operations.

```typescript
await client.dispose();
```

### `adapterInfo`

Returns the adapter name and declared capabilities.

```typescript
const info = client.adapterInfo();
// { name: "memory", capabilities: { persistent: false, searchAll: true, fuzzy: true, fieldBoosts: true } }
```

## Convenience Constructors

Shorthand for common adapter setups:

```typescript
import { createMemorySearchClient, createIndexedDbSearchClient } from "@searchfn/client";

const memoryClient = createMemorySearchClient({
  adapterConfig: { pipeline: { /* custom pipeline */ } },
  defaults: { limit: 20, fuzzy: true },
});

const browserClient = createIndexedDbSearchClient({
  adapterConfig: { dbName: "my-app-search", cache: { terms: 4096 } },
  defaults: { limit: 20, fuzzy: true },
});
```

## Validation Limits

The client validates all inputs before passing them to the adapter:

| Limit | Default |
| --- | --- |
| Max query length | `1000` characters |
| Max `limit` | `10,000` |
| Max `limitPerResource` | `1,000` |
| Max resources in `searchAll` | `50` |
| Max documents per `index` batch | `10,000` |

Validation failures throw `SearchClientValidationError` with a `code` and optional `details.path`.



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Configuration

URL: https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/configuration
Description: Full configuration tables for the server, client, and every adapter.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This page is the canonical reference. The same fields appear in narrower pages with examples — here they live as one queryable table.

## Server configuration

`createSearchFnServer(options)`:

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `adapter` | `SearchAdapter` | — | Required. Backing adapter |
| `basePath` | `string` | `"/searchfn"` | URL prefix for endpoints |
| `limits` | `Partial<ServerLimits>` | see below | Override default limits |
| `authorize` | `(ctx, action, payload) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | — | Authorization callback |
| `logger` | `SearchFnLogger` | — | Structured logger (info/warn/error/debug) |

### Server limits

| Field | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxPayloadBytes` | `1_048_576` (1 MB) | Max request body size |
| `maxQueryLength` | `1_000` | Max query string length |
| `maxResourcesPerSearchAll` | `50` | Max resources per `search-all` |
| `maxLimit` | `10_000` | Max `limit` param |
| `maxLimitPerResource` | `1_000` | Max `limitPerResource` |
| `maxIndexBatch` | `10_000` | Max docs per `index` batch |

## Client configuration

`createSearchClient(options)`:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `adapter` | `SearchAdapter` | Required |
| `defaults.limit` | `number` | Default `search` limit |
| `defaults.limitPerResource` | `number` | Default `searchAll` per-resource limit |
| `defaults.fuzzy` | `boolean \| number` | Enable fuzzy by default; number is edit distance |
| `defaults.prefix` | `boolean` | Enable prefix/edge-n-gram matching by default |
| `defaults.fields` | `string[]?` | Default field restriction |
| `defaults.fieldBoosts` | `Record<string, number>?` | Default field weights |

## Convenience client constructors

`createMemorySearchClient(options)`:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `adapterConfig.pipeline` | `Pipeline?` | Custom text pipeline |
| `adapterConfig.stopWords` | `Set<string> \| Record<string, Set<string>>` | Per-language stop words |
| `adapterConfig.diagnostics` | `DiagnosticsSink?` | Diagnostics callback |
| `defaults` | `ClientDefaults` | Same as `createSearchClient` |

`createIndexedDbSearchClient(options)`:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `adapterConfig.dbName` | `string` | IndexedDB database name |
| `adapterConfig.cache.terms` | `number` | LRU cache size for hot term lookups (default 1024) |
| `adapterConfig.cache.postings` | `number` | LRU cache size for postings (default 2048) |
| `adapterConfig.pipeline` | `Pipeline?` | Custom pipeline |
| `defaults` | `ClientDefaults` | Same as `createSearchClient` |

## Adapter configs

### `MemoryAdapter`

```typescript
new MemoryAdapter({
  pipeline,           // optional Pipeline
  stopWords,          // optional Set or per-language map
  diagnostics,        // optional sink
})
```

### `IndexedDbAdapter`

```typescript
new IndexedDbAdapter({
  dbName: "my-search",
  cache: { terms: 1024, postings: 2048 },
  pipeline,
  stopWords,
  diagnostics,
})
```

### `PostgresAdapter`

```typescript
new PostgresAdapter({
  connectionString: "postgres://...",
  schema: "public",
  tablePrefix: "_searchfn_",
  queryTimeoutMs: 15_000,
  retry: { maxRetries: 3, baseDelayMs: 200, maxDelayMs: 10_000 },
})
```

### `MeilisearchAdapter`

```typescript
new MeilisearchAdapter({
  host: "https://search.example.com",
  apiKey: process.env.MEILI_API_KEY,
  indexPrefix: "prod_",
  requestTimeoutMs: 10_000,
})
```

### `ElasticsearchAdapter` / `OpenSearchAdapter`

```typescript
new ElasticsearchAdapter({
  engine: "elasticsearch", // or "opensearch"
  node: "https://es.example.com",
  apiKey: process.env.ES_API_KEY,
  indexPrefix: "prod_",
})
```

## DataFn provider

`createSearchProvider(adapter, options)`:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resourceFields` | `Record<string, string[]>` | Which DataFn record fields to index per resource. Default: all except `id`. |

## Swift configuration

`SearchFnClientConfiguration`:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `defaults` | `SearchFnDefaults` | limit, limitPerResource, fuzzy, prefix |
| `diagnostics` | `SearchFnDiagnosticsSink?` | Opt-in event sink |

`SearchFnSQLiteAdapterConfiguration`:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rootURL` | `URL` | Storage root |
| `indexKey` | `String` | Unique key for this index (hashed for directory name) |
| `pipeline` | `SearchFnPipeline?` | Custom pipeline |
| `diagnostics` | `SearchFnDiagnosticsSink?` | Diagnostics |

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Envelopes

URL: https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/envelopes
Description: Canonical SearchFn request and response envelopes.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The SearchFn HTTP server wraps every response in a discriminated union envelope. Clients (TypeScript, Python, Swift, or your own) parse the envelope first, then descend into `result` or `error`.

## Response envelope

```typescript
type Envelope<T> =
  | { ok: true; result: T }
  | { ok: false; error: ErrorBody };

type ErrorBody = {
  code: string;
  message: string;
  details?: Record<string, unknown>;
};
```

### Success

```json
{ "ok": true, "result": { "ids": ["t-1", "t-3"] } }
```

The shape of `result` depends on the operation:

| Operation | `result` shape |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | `{ adapter: string, capabilities: SearchAdapterCapabilities, uptimeMs: number }` |
| `index` | `{ indexed: number }` |
| `search` | `{ ids: Array<string \| number> }` |
| `searchAll` | `{ results: Array<{ resource, id, score }> }` |
| `remove` | `{ removed: number }` |
| `clear` | `{ cleared: string }` |

### Failure

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
    "message": "documents exceeds maxIndexBatch (10000)",
    "details": { "path": "documents", "actual": 12000, "max": 10000 }
  }
}
```

`details.path` always points to the offending field (`query`, `resource`, `documents`, etc.) where applicable.

## Request envelopes

Requests are plain JSON — there's no wrapping object. Each operation has its own shape; see the per-endpoint pages in [Server reference](/docs/reference/server).

Example:

```json
{
  "resource": "articles",
  "query": "search ranking",
  "limit": 10,
  "fuzzy": true,
  "fields": ["title", "body"],
  "fieldBoosts": { "title": 2.0 }
}
```

## Content type

All requests must set `Content-Type: application/json`. Responses are always `application/json`. The server returns `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`.

## HTTP status codes

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful operation |
| 400 | Validation failure (`DFQL_INVALID`, `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `DFQL_UNSUPPORTED`) |
| 403 | Authorization denied (`FORBIDDEN`) |
| 499 | Client aborted (`DFQL_ABORTED`) |
| 500 | Backend or runtime failure (`INTERNAL`, `SEARCH_ADAPTER_DISPOSED`) |
| 504 | Operation timed out (`SEARCH_TIMEOUT`) |

`499` follows nginx's convention for "client closed request" — useful for log filtering.

## Idempotency

Index and remove operations are idempotent on `(resource, id)` — re-sending the same document is safe. Indexing the same ID twice updates the row; removing an already-removed ID returns `removed: 0` and `ok: true`.

`clear` is destructive but idempotent — calling it twice on an empty resource is a no-op.

## Versioning

The envelope shape is part of the public API contract. Breaking changes go through a major version bump with both shapes accepted for one minor's deprecation window.

## See also

- [Server reference](/docs/reference/server)
- [Errors](/docs/reference/errors)
- [Configuration](/docs/reference/configuration)



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Errors

URL: https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/errors
Description: All SearchFn error codes — cause, fix, and retry semantics.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Every SearchFn response is an envelope. Failures look like:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "DFQL_INVALID",
    "message": "Query must be a non-empty string",
    "details": { "path": "query" }
  }
}
```

## Error matrix

| Code | HTTP | Cause | Fix | Retry? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DFQL_INVALID` | 400 | Malformed request, missing required fields, wrong types | Validate the request shape client-side; check `details.path` | No |
| `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 400 | Query/limit/batch size above the server's configured max | Reduce request size or increase `limits` in `createSearchFnServer` | No |
| `DFQL_ABORTED` | 499 | The caller aborted via `AbortSignal` before the operation completed | None — this is the expected outcome of cancellation | No |
| `DFQL_UNSUPPORTED` | 400 | The adapter doesn't implement the requested operation or option | Check adapter capabilities; use a different adapter; drop the unsupported option | No |
| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | The `authorize` callback returned false | Verify credentials / role | No |
| `INTERNAL` | 500 | Unexpected backend failure | Inspect logs; check backend health; retry with backoff | Yes |
| `SEARCH_ADAPTER_DISPOSED` | 500 | Called any method after `dispose()` | Re-initialize the adapter before use | No |
| `SEARCH_TIMEOUT` | 504 | Adapter operation exceeded its timeout | Increase the adapter's `queryTimeoutMs`; check backend latency | Yes |

## Client-side validation errors

The client throws `SearchClientValidationError` before making any network call:

```typescript
try {
  await client.search({ resource: "tasks", query: "" });
} catch (err) {
  if (err.code === "DFQL_INVALID") {
    console.error("path:", err.details?.path); // "query"
  }
}
```

Validation never reaches the server, which means these errors are free of network latency and trivially testable.

## Per-adapter error patterns

### MemoryAdapter / IndexedDbAdapter

These run in-process. Errors are almost always `DFQL_INVALID` (bad request) or `SEARCH_ADAPTER_DISPOSED`. `INTERNAL` indicates a bug in the built-in engine — file an issue.

### PostgresAdapter

| Symptom | Likely code | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `connection refused` | `INTERNAL` | DB unreachable or auth wrong |
| Missing table | `INTERNAL` | Migration didn't run; see [Postgres adapter migration](/docs/reference/adapters/postgres) |
| Long-running query | `SEARCH_TIMEOUT` | Tune `queryTimeoutMs` |
| Retry exhaustion | `INTERNAL` (after retries) | Tune `retry.maxRetries` / inspect DB health |

### Meilisearch / Elasticsearch / OpenSearch

| Symptom | Likely code | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bad API key | `INTERNAL` (with backend body in logs) | Rotate credentials |
| Index missing | `INTERNAL` | Call `initialize()` to create indexes |
| Network blip | `INTERNAL` | Retried automatically per adapter config |
| Wrong engine string | `DFQL_UNSUPPORTED` | Set `engine: "elasticsearch"` or `"opensearch"` |

## Retry semantics

Only `INTERNAL`, `SEARCH_TIMEOUT`, and transient backend errors are safe to retry. Use exponential backoff:

```typescript
async function withRetry<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>, max = 3): Promise<T> {
  let lastErr;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < max; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (err: any) {
      if (err.code !== "INTERNAL" && err.code !== "SEARCH_TIMEOUT") throw err;
      lastErr = err;
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100 * Math.pow(2, attempt) + Math.random() * 100));
    }
  }
  throw lastErr;
}
```

Adapters that talk to external backends (Postgres, Meilisearch, ES/OS) already retry internally; don't double-retry at the application layer.

## See also

- [Envelopes](/docs/reference/envelopes)
- [Events](/docs/reference/events)
- [Troubleshooting](/docs/operations/troubleshooting)



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Events

URL: https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/events
Description: Server log events and Swift diagnostics events.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

SearchFn emits structured events from two surfaces: the TypeScript server's `logger`, and the Swift `SearchFnDiagnosticsSink`. Both are opt-in and field-redacted by default.

## TypeScript server events

Pass a `logger` to `createSearchFnServer`:

```typescript
const sf = await createSearchFnServer({
  adapter,
  logger: {
    info: (msg, ctx) => console.log(JSON.stringify({ level: "info", msg, ...ctx })),
    warn: (msg, ctx) => console.warn(JSON.stringify({ level: "warn", msg, ...ctx })),
    error: (msg, ctx) => console.error(JSON.stringify({ level: "error", msg, ...ctx })),
    debug: (msg, ctx) => console.debug(JSON.stringify({ level: "debug", msg, ...ctx })),
  },
});
```

### Event names

| Event | Emitted when | Level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `request.start` | Inbound request enters the router | info |
| `request.end` | Request completes successfully | info |
| `request.error` | Request fails (any error code) | error |
| `authorization.denied` | `authorize` returned `false` | warn |
| `authorization.error` | `authorize` threw | error |
| `server.close` | `close()` was called on the server | info |

### Context fields

Every event carries:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `operation` | `string` | `status`, `index`, `search`, `searchAll`, `remove`, `clear` |
| `adapter` | `string` | Adapter name (`memory`, `postgres`, `meilisearch`, etc.) |
| `durationMs` | `number` | Operation duration |
| `status` | `number` | HTTP status code |
| `success` | `boolean` | True for `request.end`, false for `request.error` |
| `errorCode` | `string?` | Set on failures |
| `requestId` | `string?` | Inherited from inbound request headers |

### Secret redaction

These keys are recursively redacted before being passed to the logger:

`apiKey`, `password`, `secret`, `token`, `authorization`, `connectionString`

This applies to the payload context that's attached to events; the logger never sees raw credentials.

## Swift diagnostics events

```swift
let sink = SearchFnDiagnosticsSink { event in
    switch event {
    case .client(let group, let detail):
        log("client.\(group):", detail)
    case .adapter(let group, let detail):
        log("adapter.\(group):", detail)
    case .persistence(let group, let detail):
        log("persistence.\(group):", detail)
    }
}

let client = search.client(configuration: SearchFnClientConfiguration(diagnostics: sink))
```

### Groups

**Client groups:**
`initialize`, `index`, `search`, `searchAll`, `searchAll.fallback`, `remove`, `clear`, `dispose`

**Adapter groups:**
`initialize`, `index`, `search`, `searchAll`, `remove`, `clear`, `dispose`

**Persistence groups:**
`open`, `reopen`, `close`

### What's in a diagnostics event

Counts and metadata: resource names, query length, document count per index batch, index key, deterministic directory name, schema version. Raw query strings and indexed field values are **not** included by design — diagnostics are safe to log.

## Aggregating into observability tools

### Datadog

```typescript
const dd = new TracingApi();

const sf = await createSearchFnServer({
  adapter,
  logger: {
    info: (msg, ctx) => dd.send({ message: msg, ...ctx, service: "searchfn" }),
    warn: (msg, ctx) => dd.send({ message: msg, level: "warn", ...ctx, service: "searchfn" }),
    error: (msg, ctx) => dd.send({ message: msg, level: "error", ...ctx, service: "searchfn" }),
    debug: () => {},
  },
});
```

### OpenTelemetry

Wrap each handler to start a span; emit `searchfn` span attributes from the event context fields. Search latency goes on `durationMs`; status code on `http.status_code`.

## See also

- [Server reference](/docs/reference/server)
- [Errors](/docs/reference/errors)
- [Observability](/docs/operations/observability)



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Python Reference

URL: https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/python
Description: API reference for the Python SearchFn package.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Python SearchFn package is a lightweight, database-backed search engine designed as a DataFn companion. It stores its inverted index in the same database as your DataFn data — no extra infrastructure for small to medium apps.

## Install

```bash
pip install searchfn
```

## `create_searchfn_server(config)`

Creates the server plugin definitions for mounting into an HTTP framework.

```python
from searchfn import create_searchfn_server
from datafn.db import PostgresAdapter

search_plugin = create_searchfn_server({
    "schema": schema,        # DataFn schema dict
    "db": db,                # DataFn DB adapter instance
    "table_prefix": "_searchfn_",  # optional
})
```

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | `dict` | yes | DataFn schema object |
| `db` | DB adapter | yes | DataFn-compatible DB adapter (Postgres, SQLite) |
| `table_prefix` | `str` | no | Prefix for SearchFn-owned tables. Default: `_searchfn_` |

**Returns:** `dict` with `routes` key — a map of HTTP paths to async handlers.

## HTTP endpoints

When mounted, the plugin exposes:

### `POST /searchfn/index`

Triggers (re-)indexing of a model or all models.

**Request:**

```json
{ "model": "products" }
```

Omit `model` to index all string fields across all resources.

**Response:**

```json
{ "ok": true, "result": { "totalIndexed": 1234 } }
```

### `POST /searchfn/search`

Searches the inverted index.

**Request:**

```json
{ "query": "fast laptop", "model": "products", "limit": 20 }
```

`model` is optional; omit to search across all indexed models.

**Response:**

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "results": [
    { "id": "p-1", "model": "products", "score": 1.42 },
    { "id": "p-7", "model": "products", "score": 0.88 }
  ]
}
```

## Core functions

### `index_data(schema, db, model=None, table_prefix="_searchfn_")`

Indexes records into the search table. Use for background indexing jobs.

```python
import asyncio
from searchfn import index_data

async def reindex():
    await index_data(schema, db, model="products")

asyncio.run(reindex())
```

### `search_index(schema, db, query, model=None, limit=20, table_prefix="_searchfn_")`

Search programmatically. Returns matching records sorted by relevance.

```python
import asyncio
from searchfn import search_index

async def go():
    results = await search_index(schema, db, query="fast laptop")
    for r in results:
        print(r["id"], r["model"], r["score"])

asyncio.run(go())
```

## How it works

The Python package maintains an inverted index in a single table (default `_searchfn_index`):

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `term` | A token from the indexed text |
| `model` | The DataFn resource name |
| `record_id` | The record's ID |
| `field` | Which field this term came from |

Search scoring is based on the number of matching terms per record. The package is intentionally simple — for richer ranking (BM25, fuzzy, field boosts), use the TypeScript server's `PostgresAdapter`, which writes a tsvector-backed index, and call it from Python over HTTP.

## When to choose which Python path

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Quick MVP, DataFn already on Postgres/SQLite | Python `create_searchfn_server` |
| Production-grade ranking, BM25 | TypeScript `@searchfn/server` + `PostgresAdapter`, called over HTTP |
| Browser local search | TypeScript `@searchfn/adapter-indexeddb` |

## See also

- [FastAPI quickstart](/docs/quickstart/fastapi)
- [Starlette quickstart](/docs/quickstart/starlette)
- [Flask quickstart](/docs/quickstart/flask)



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Server API

URL: https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/server
Description: Expose SearchFn as an HTTP API with authorization, logging, and secret redaction.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Creating a Server

Use `createSearchFnServer()` to wrap any adapter behind HTTP endpoints.

```typescript
import { createSearchFnServer } from "@searchfn/server";
import { PostgresAdapter } from "@searchfn/adapter-postgres";

const server = await createSearchFnServer({
  adapter: new PostgresAdapter({
    connectionString: process.env.SEARCH_DB_URL!,
  }),
  basePath: "/searchfn",
  authorize: async (ctx, action, payload) => {
    return ctx.user?.role === "admin" || action === "search" || action === "status";
  },
});

// Mount server.router with your HTTP framework adapter
```

## Configuration

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `adapter` | `SearchAdapter` | — | Required. The search adapter to use. |
| `basePath` | `string` | `"/searchfn"` | URL prefix for all endpoints. |
| `limits` | `Partial<ServerLimits>` | See below | Override default validation limits. |
| `authorize` | `(ctx, action, payload) => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | — | Per-action authorization callback. |
| `logger` | `SearchFnLogger` | — | Custom structured logger. |

### Server Limits

| Limit | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxPayloadBytes` | `1,048,576` | Maximum request body size (1 MB). |
| `maxQueryLength` | `1,000` | Maximum search query string length. |
| `maxResourcesPerSearchAll` | `50` | Maximum resources in a `searchAll` request. |
| `maxLimit` | `10,000` | Maximum `limit` parameter. |
| `maxLimitPerResource` | `1,000` | Maximum `limitPerResource` parameter. |
| `maxIndexBatch` | `10,000` | Maximum documents per `index` request. |

## Endpoints

All endpoints are prefixed with the configured `basePath`.

### `GET /searchfn/status`

Health check and adapter information.

**Response:**
```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "result": {
    "adapter": "postgres",
    "capabilities": { "persistent": true, "searchAll": true, "fuzzy": true },
    "uptimeMs": 84200
  }
}
```

### `POST /searchfn/index`

Index documents into a resource.

**Request:**
```json
{
  "resource": "tasks",
  "documents": [
    { "id": "t-1", "fields": { "title": "Ship docs", "description": "Write the guide" } }
  ]
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{ "ok": true, "result": { "indexed": 1 } }
```

### `POST /searchfn/search`

Search a single resource.

**Request:**
```json
{
  "resource": "tasks",
  "query": "docs",
  "limit": 10,
  "fuzzy": true,
  "fields": ["title"],
  "fieldBoosts": { "title": 2.0 }
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{ "ok": true, "result": { "ids": ["t-1", "t-3"] } }
```

### `POST /searchfn/search-all`

Search across multiple resources.

**Request:**
```json
{
  "query": "docs",
  "resources": ["tasks", "notes"],
  "limitPerResource": 5
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "result": {
    "results": [
      { "resource": "tasks", "id": "t-1", "score": 1.5 },
      { "resource": "notes", "id": "n-2", "score": 0.9 }
    ]
  }
}
```

### `POST /searchfn/remove`

Remove documents by ID.

**Request:**
```json
{ "resource": "tasks", "ids": ["t-1", "t-2"] }
```

**Response:**
```json
{ "ok": true, "result": { "removed": 2 } }
```

### `POST /searchfn/clear`

Clear all documents from a resource.

**Request:**
```json
{ "resource": "tasks" }
```

**Response:**
```json
{ "ok": true, "result": { "cleared": "tasks" } }
```

## Authorization

The `authorize` callback is called before every operation. It receives the request context, action name, and request payload:

```typescript
const server = await createSearchFnServer({
  adapter,
  authorize: async (ctx, action, payload) => {
    if (action === "status") return true;
    if (action === "search" || action === "searchAll") return !!ctx.user;
    return ctx.user?.role === "admin";
  },
});
```

| Action | When called |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | `GET /searchfn/status` |
| `index` | `POST /searchfn/index` |
| `search` | `POST /searchfn/search` |
| `searchAll` | `POST /searchfn/search-all` |
| `remove` | `POST /searchfn/remove` |
| `clear` | `POST /searchfn/clear` |

Denied requests return a `FORBIDDEN` error envelope.

## Structured Logging

Pass a `logger` to receive structured log events for every operation:

```typescript
const server = await createSearchFnServer({
  adapter,
  logger: {
    info: (msg, ctx) => console.log(msg, ctx),
    warn: (msg, ctx) => console.warn(msg, ctx),
    error: (msg, ctx) => console.error(msg, ctx),
    debug: (msg, ctx) => console.debug(msg, ctx),
  },
});
```

Log context includes: `operation`, `adapter`, `durationMs`, `status`, `success`, and `errorCode` (on failure). Sensitive values (`apiKey`, `password`, `connectionString`, `token`, `authorization`, `secret`) are recursively redacted.

## Closing the Server

Call `close()` to shut down the server and dispose of the adapter:

```typescript
await server.close();
```



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Swift Package Reference

URL: https://searchfn.com/docs/reference/swift
Description: Reference for the standalone SearchFn Swift package, adapters, convenience APIs, and diagnostics.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Products

| Product | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `SearchFnCore` | Built-in search engine primitives |
| `SearchFnAdapterContracts` | Shared request/response/config/error types |
| `SearchFnMemoryAdapter` | Ephemeral in-memory local search |
| `SearchFnSQLiteAdapter` | Persisted SearchFn-owned local search |
| `SearchFnClient` | Validating client facade |
| `SearchFnConvenience` | `InMemorySearchFn` and `SearchFn(sqlite:)` |

## Convenience APIs

### `InMemorySearchFn`

Use for local, process-owned search state:

```swift
let search = InMemorySearchFn()
let client = search.client()
```

### `SearchFn(sqlite:)`

Use for persisted local search state:

```swift
let search = try SearchFn(
    sqlite: SearchFnSQLiteAdapterConfiguration(
        rootURL: rootURL,
        indexKey: "project-docs"
    )
)
```

## Client Methods

The Swift client mirrors the SearchFn adapter/client contract semantics:

- `initialize(_:)`
- `index(_:)`
- `search(_:)`
- `searchAll(_:)`
- `remove(resource:ids:)`
- `clear(resource:)`
- `dispose()`
- `adapterInfo()`

Deterministic `searchAll` ordering is:

1. `score desc`
2. `resource asc`
3. `id asc`

## Diagnostics

Diagnostics are opt-in and use `SearchFnDiagnosticsEvent`.

Current event groups include:

- `client.initialize`
- `client.index`
- `client.search`
- `client.searchAll`
- `client.searchAll.fallback`
- `client.remove`
- `client.clear`
- `client.dispose`
- `adapter.initialize`
- `adapter.index`
- `adapter.search`
- `adapter.searchAll`
- `adapter.remove`
- `adapter.clear`
- `adapter.dispose`
- `persistence.open`
- `persistence.reopen`
- `persistence.close`

Diagnostics include counts and metadata such as resource names, query length, index key, deterministic directory name, and schema version. They intentionally omit raw query bodies and indexed field contents.

## Persistence Ownership

`SearchFnSQLiteAdapter` stores SearchFn-owned search state beneath the caller-supplied root directory. It does not place index state in Core Data.

Persisted contents include:

- resource configuration
- stored documents
- postings
- vocabulary counts
- posting metadata
- manifest format metadata
